1.concept: A doubly linked list adds a second pointer to every node: `prev`, pointing backward to the previous node, alongside the `next` pointer pointing forward. This lets you walk the list in either direction, at the cost of one extra pointer to keep correct on every insert and delete. The payoff isn't just direction, though — it's what deletion costs. In a singly linked list, deleting a node you already have a reference to still means walking from the head to find its predecessor, because you need to rewire the node before it; that's O(n). With `prev` already in hand, the doubly linked list makes that same deletion O(1) — you can jump straight to the predecessor without a search.
1.analogy: A singly linked list is a one-way hallway with doors that only open forward. A doubly linked list adds doors that also open backward — but now every door has two hinges to maintain instead of one, and forgetting one hinge leaves a door that looks fine walking forward but breaks the moment you turn around.
1.mascotDialogue: Same idea as before, just one more pointer per node. The catch: every insert now has FOUR pointers to update, not two. Miss one, and the list looks fine in one direction and broken in the other.
